why: A precise reference for using type as the transition object: background letters rotate, scale, and move forward to preserve continuity between navigation states.

compositions.title: Letters carry the page change
compositions.study: The transition gives typography identity across screens instead of crossfading unrelated layouts.
compositions.reuse: Use when a portfolio, editorial, or campaign microsite needs navigation to feel authored.

compositions.title: Final typographic still frame
compositions.study: The motion path resolves into a readable next screen, so the animated idea is not separate from content.
compositions.reuse: Design the destination composition first, then choreograph the transition into it.

assets.notes: The reusable idea is a staged timeline: background type gains prominence, moves, then reveals new content.
assets.reuse: Document phases, delays, and interruption rules before implementation.

assets.notes: Navigation must work without relying on rotating or zooming type.
assets.reuse: Use instant page change or subtle opacity/position changes for reduced-motion users.

motion.title: Foregrounding background letters
motion.notes: Large letters become spatial objects that bridge old and new content.
motion.fallback: Keep a static title lockup and standard page transition.

interactions.title: Click-triggered page reveal
interactions.study: The interaction begins on item selection and makes the next screen feel connected to the chosen content.
interactions.reuse: Use for small sets of high-value destinations, not routine dense navigation.

implementation.notes: Useful for campaign microsites, portfolios, editorial chapters, and immersive menu transitions.
